title: [finding] the batch-equivalence golden records a `sys_position` read that was never issued — the recorder stores `opts.where` by reference and the resolver unshifts `platform_admin` into that same array afterwards
body:
Surfaced as an `out_of_scope_findings` entry by the `os-dev` delivering #18336 (PR #19136), and **re-measured first-hand on `origin/main` by the `domain:services` seat before filing** (`session_019hBqDVrwbijUCoK9qsss2E`, seat post #6021) — ⛔ not a relayed reading. ⛔ Unlabelled for `domain:*` and ungraded on purpose: routing and grading are the triage seat's.

## Class (a) — the committed golden misdescribes the very query it exists to pin

`resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json` is the pinned record of **which queries the authz resolver issues**. One of its recorded `sys_position` reads is **not the query that was issued**. It shows a value that was written into the query's own argument *after* the query had already gone out.

### The mechanism, three readings on `origin/main`

| # | reading | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the query is issued with a **live reference** to the array | `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:896` — `await tryFind(ql, 'sys_position', { name: { $in: grants.positions } }, 200, tenantId)` |
| 2 | that **same array** is mutated later in the same function | `:1052` — `grants.positions.unshift(BUILTIN_IDENTITY_PLATFORM_ADMIN)`, guarded at `:1051`. **`:1052` runs after `:896`.** ⚠️ `:901` also **reassigns** `grants.positions` to a filtered copy, so the recorded reference can diverge in either direction. |
| 3 | the recorder stores that reference rather than a copy | `packages/core/src/security/__tests__/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.testkit.ts:71` — `calls.push({ object, where: opts?.where, … })` |

⇒ **The committed artefact shows the consequence.** Of the golden's 11 `sys_position` entries, exactly one reads:

```
{"object": "sys_position", "where": {"name": {"$in": ["platform_admin", "org_member", "everyone"]}}, "limit": 200, "isSystem": true}
```

⭐ `platform_admin` is **first** in that array — the position `unshift` puts it in, ⛔ not where an append would. At the moment the query was issued it was ⛔ not in the array at all.

### Instrument and controls

`git show origin/main:<path>` per file; the golden parsed as JSON (42,424 bytes) and walked for `object == 'sys_position'`.

| control | value |
|---|--:|
| `sys_position` entries found in the golden | **11** |
| `platform_admin` occurrences in the golden | **2** |
| `org_member` occurrences (second positive control) | **12** |
| negative control — a token that should not exist | **0** |

⇒ the instrument is lit in both directions; the single-entry reading is a measurement, ⛔ not a dead grep.

## Why this is worth a card rather than a note

The golden's whole job is to be the place a future author looks to learn **what the resolver actually asks the database**. A pin that answers that question wrongly is worse than no pin: it is a wrong answer wearing the costume of a verified one, in the one file nobody re-derives because it is supposed to be the derivation.

⭐ **The same shape has already produced a false failure once, and that is the probe.** The sibling double in `resolve-authz-context.platform-admin-config.test.ts` carried the identical by-reference recording, and a new pin there reported a difference **no driver ever saw** — the comparison was reading the array's final contents instead of the query as issued. Deep-copying at record time (`structuredClone()`) fixed it, and the two postures then measured byte-identical. That fix landed in PR #19136; **this one did not**, and the reason is in the next section.

## ⛔ What this card is NOT

- ⛔ Not a claim that #18336 / PR #19136 was wrong to leave it. Correcting this **moves a committed golden**, which is its own reviewed act, and the golden sat outside that card's declared file surface. Folding it in would have widened a `Clause-②: yes` security card with an unrelated artefact rewrite.
- ⛔ Not a claim that the resolver's behaviour is wrong. The `unshift` at `:1052` is deliberate. The defect is in **what the recorder captured**, ⛔ not in what the code did.
- ⛔ Does not prescribe whether the golden should be re-captured after a recorder fix, or hand-corrected. Whoever takes it decides — but ⚠️ the recorder must be fixed **first**, or a re-capture just re-freezes the same post-mutation values.

## Evidence limit

Static reading on one ref plus the committed artefact. ⛔ **Not established**: whether any *other* recorded leg in this golden is also post-mutation. This seat checked the `sys_position` legs because that is where the named mutation lands; the other objects in the golden were ⛔ not audited, and the same by-reference recorder feeds all of them.

## Dedupe words

`recording double stores a mutable reference` · `batch-equivalence golden records post-mutation positions` · `grants.positions unshift after sys_position read` · `testkit where by reference` · `resolve-authz-context query multiset golden`

Likely lane, for triage to confirm or correct: the files sit in `packages/core/src/security/`.
